dataset_notes: IMPORTANT: pair_01's two PDFs are NOT sequential revisions of a single drawing. They are two distinct (but structurally similar) P&ID sheets: 'Export Gas Compressor' vs 'Lift Gas Compressor'. This was discovered during review and is documented candidly here rather than hidden.

Because of that, the true structural delta between the two documents is large (hundreds of distinct tag/number differences, e.g. 26-PIT-9087 vs 26-PIT-9077, 26-000001-001 vs 26-000006-001) rather than a handful of localized edits a real revision pair would show.

This ground truth is a hand-verified SAMPLE of real, checkable differences extracted directly from `pdftotext -layout` output of both PDFs (see IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and REVIEW.md for provenance), not an exhaustive labeling of every difference. It is intended to validate that the delta engine correctly detects and classifies real, known changes -- precision/recall against this sample will still read low relative to the ~900+ raw items the engine reports, because the engine is (correctly) also detecting the hundreds of un-labeled real differences between two genuinely different documents.

For a defensible 'sensible on their own eval set' delta-quality story, the honest framing is: the alignment/classification logic works on verified real changes (see items below), but pair_01 is the wrong sample to prove 'revision delta' behavior -- a synthesized true revision pair (edit one PDF, re-export) would be a stronger eval fixture. See REVIEW.md section 5, item 5.
